name: Phygelus
overview: Phygelus is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament who is noted for having turned away from the Apostle Paul while in Asia. There is no information recorded about his tribe or any additional personal details. His mention is brief and focused solely on this act of desertion.
namesAndTitles: Phygelus is the only name recorded for this individual, and there is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to it in the biblical text. The name appears as a proper name in 2 Timothy 1:15 without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Phygelus beyond his noted action of turning away from Paul. There are no other relational details provided in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Phygelus is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of those who abandoned Paul during his ministry in Asia. His turning away highlights the challenges and opposition faced by early Christian leaders. This mention serves as a sober reminder of the cost of discipleship and the reality of apostasy within the early church.
